beats.say: You gave the right answer. And you still got no offer.
Why? The interviewer could not write down proof that you are senior.
beats.label: The reason
beats.head: No written proof of seniority

beats.say: This track fixes that with three habits: show signal, talk out loud, and use numbers.
beats.label: Track 1 · The senior loop playbook

check.prompt: Your answer was correct, but you said almost nothing. How does the round count?
check.why: The interviewer writes down evidence. With no evidence, the report is weak, even if you were right.

beats.say: First: how is a senior loop scored?
Each interviewer writes a short report. A group reads those reports and decides.
beats.label: After your rounds
beats.head: Written feedback decides

beats.say: So a round with no clear evidence counts as a weak round. Even if you were right.
beats.label: The rule
beats.head: No evidence means a weak round

beats.say: Second: what does senior signal sound like?
A mid-level answer solves the task. A senior answer also explains the trade-off.
beats.label: The difference
beats.head: Solve it, then explain the trade-off

beats.say: Ask about scale first. Name the failure cases. And say what you would monitor.
beats.label: Three easy signals

check.prompt: What is the first step of every round?
check.why: Clarify first. Then state the plan, build it, and test it.

beats.say: Third: run every round out loud.
Clarify the question. State your plan. Build it. Then test it with an edge case.
beats.label: One structure for every round

beats.say: Silence gives the interviewer nothing to write. So think in words.
beats.label: Remember
beats.head: Silence writes nothing

beats.say: Last: know a few numbers by heart.
One day has about 86,400 seconds. Round it to 100,000 for quick maths.
With that, you can turn events per day into events per second, in your head.
beats.label: Why it helps
beats.head: Per day to per second, fast

beats.say: Leave written evidence. Explain the trade-off. And run the round out loud, with numbers.
beats.label: The playbook

beats.say: Now start the first lesson below.
